title: data-cap Flow Model
description: Canonical, versioned function-level, field-sensitive data-flow facts (nodes, edges, explicit unknowns and a coverage summary), each with an epistemic status (see ADR 0070, ADR 0071). Generated from src/flow/flow-model.ts's FlowModel type -- never hand-authored.

unknowns.description: Every explicit unknown, ordered by id.

coverage.description: What was and was not analyzed.

edgeTags.description: What the scanner saw happen to the data of some edges, ordered by id. Absent when it saw nothing worth noting (ADR 0075).

scope.description: Root-relative POSIX path of the file that declares this node, or a stable namespace for a node with no file (a boundary).

source.description: Declaration position within `scope`, when there is one.

classification.description: Declared or inherited sensitivity classification, when known -- carried verbatim, never inferred here.

boundaryKind.description: What kind of boundary this is; only meaningful (and required by policy evaluation) on a `boundary` node.

FlowNode.description: One node of the Flow Model.

FlowStatus.description: ADR 0071: the five epistemic statuses, shared by every flow fact, claim and finding.

SourcePosition.description: A 1-based line/column within a file already known from context (e.g. `DependencyEdge.from`).

FlowBoundaryKind.description: What a data-flow rule can name as a destination: the declared endpoint kinds, plus the two destinations only code analysis can see.

DataFlowEndpointKind.description: What kind of boundary a declared data-flow endpoint crosses -- a data store (`database`/`cache`/`storage`/`queue`), an external entity (`api`/`external-service`/`user-input`), or something internal to this codebase (`computed`/`internal`).

path.description: The field path this edge carries, for a field-sensitive edge; absent for an edge about the whole value or about control.

source.description: Where in source this edge arises (a call site, a read), when known.

handling.description: The data-safety state of the value at this hop, when declared or established -- policy evaluation reads it at boundary crossings.

origin.description: Id of the `field` node whose data this edge carries. Present on every data-carrying edge the flow pass derives, so a helper shared by several fields does not make each field appear to reach every other field's destinations. Absent on edges that are not about one field's data (a `calls` edge). `path` is expressed in the origin field's frame.

FlowEdge.description: One edge of the Flow Model.

FlowEdgeKind.description: What an edge means. Data moves `from` -> `to` along `reads`, `writes`, `transforms`, `passes`, `returns` and `crosses-boundary`; `calls` is control flow and `discards` records that a function received a field and deliberately did not forward it -- neither carries data, so tracing does not follow them. `side-effect` links a function to the boundary it acts on.

SourceLocation.description: A `SourcePosition` plus the file it's in, for anywhere the file isn't already implied by the surrounding structure (e.g. a finding's list of candidate sites spanning multiple files).

FlowHandling.description: The declared data-safety state of a value at a boundary crossing -- the vocabulary of `DataFlowEndpoint.handling` and of flow policy rules.

subject.description: The node this unknown prevents us from fully describing, when there is one.

origin.description: Id of the `field` node the data comes from.

path.description: Path inside the field; `[]` is the whole field.

items.description: A piece of capability-field data an unknown concerns: the field node and the path inside it.

data.description: The tracked data that entered the part of the program that could not be followed. Absent means "unknown which data" -- every trace that reaches the subject must treat itself as incomplete. Present, it lets a trace of a different field or an unrelated path stay complete: an opaque call that only ever saw `email` says nothing about where `passwordHash` went.

FlowUnknown.description: An explicit record that part of the program could not be analyzed.

FlowUnknownReason.description: Why a part of the program could not be analyzed (ADR 0053 citations apply to each).

functionsAnalyzed.description: Function nodes whose status is not `unknown`.

complete.description: True only when nothing above is non-zero apart from `functionsAnalyzed`.

FlowCoverage.description: What was and was not analyzed -- a projection must not call a graph complete unless `complete`.

edge.description: Id of the existing edge that carries the data at this place (an edge id as `flowEdgeId` derives it).

source.description: Where the copy, the derivation or the hand-over is.

fresh.description: With `copy`: the value copied was already a fresh copy.

unused.description: With `derive`: nothing ever reads the derived value.

FlowEdgeTag.description: One tag of the Flow Model.

FlowVia.description:
What the scanner saw happen to the data of an edge at one place, beyond what the edge says (ADR 0075).

- `serialize-roundtrip`: the data was taken apart and put back together with nothing in between that reads it (`JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x))`, `Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(x))`).
- `copy`: the data was copied and nothing was added, dropped or renamed (`structuredClone(x)`, `{...x }`, `[...x]`, `Array.from(x)`). `fresh` says the copied value was itself a copy made by one of these.
- `derive`: a value computed from the data was bound to a name that is never read (`unused`).
- `forward`: reserved for a producer that knows a function only hands the data on. The scanner does not emit it; forwarding chains are found from the edges alone, so no reader depends on this tag.
